 ITR Filing Deadline: This revised date gives additional time to such taxpayers to complete the process for Assessment Year (AY) 2026-27. 
 Written By Sheetal Prasad 
 Updated: Nov 4, 2026, 14:56 IST Follow us Join us Preferred source Select  News24 ITR Filing Deadline extended to November 21
 ITR Filing Deadline: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has extended the deadline for filing income tax returns (ITR) for AY 2026-27 from October 31 to November 21, 2026. Businesses, professionals, and eligible taxpayers whose accounts require a statutory audit now have additional time. The deadline, however, doesn’t allow extra time for all income tax filers. 
 Advertisement ITR filing deadline: Who is eligible?
 The November 21 deadline for ITR filing applies to taxpayers who come under the tax audit provisions of the Income Tax Act. It also applies to partners of a company whose accounts have been audited, where appropriate.
 Advertisement This revised date gives additional time to such taxpayers to complete the process for Assessment Year (AY) 2026-27. The extended date does not cover individuals who do not fall into these categories.
 Businesses must complete this before filing ITR
 This extra time is particularly pertinent for organisations that are yet to complete audit and tax documentation. Businesses should check the numbers they have reported in the Income Tax Returns against their books of account and financial statements before filing.
 Advertisement It can include reviewing income and spending amounts, reconciling financial records, or examining tax audit reports and disclosures. There could be variations between the accounting records and the details in tax-related documents that the firm needs to address.
 What taxpayers needs to know?
 Taxpayers must prioritize these tasks before November 21 deadline: 
 Advertisement 
 Complete unfinished audits before the deadline
 Ensure financial statements are reconciled
 Double-check tax calculations before filing the return
 Verify supporting documents, reports, and records 
 Pay outstanding self-assessment tax liability before filing ITR
 Taxpayers should check whether any interest provisions apply to their specific situations
